description: Mercure hub: build identity, uptime and config-reload status, subscribers, publish rate and failures, disconnect-reason breakdown, claim-binding rejections, subscribers by binding value, SSE write latency, and Caddy/Go/process runtime metrics. Provisioned and locked (`editable: false`) — UI edits won't persist; fork via the dashboard menu's Save As for local experiments, or edit `grafana/dashboards/hub.json` and re-provision. The metric reference is docs/production/metrics.md. Network throughput (process_network_*) is exported on Linux only.

links.title: Redis Transport
links.tooltip: Redis transport metrics (dispatch, publish, XREADGROUP, history replay, pool) — only populated when redistransport is the configured transport

panels.title: Hub version (fork)
panels.description: Fork build version (lzrf0cuz/mercure). Each instance shows as a separate row; mixed values during a rolling deploy are visible.

panels.title: Upstream version
panels.description: dunglas/mercure tag this fork was built against. Empty when built outside the fork's Taskfile/Dockerfile pipeline. Each instance shows as a separate row; mixed values during a rolling deploy are visible.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Process uptime since the most recent restart across selected instances (min so the freshest restart is what's surfaced).

panels.title: Subscribers connected
panels.description: Currently-connected subscriber count (instantaneous, per instance — pick a single $instance for one row, or All to compare replicas). After an applied Caddy config reload the gauge excludes subscribers held over from the previous config until they disconnect.

panels.title: Last config reload
panels.description: Status of the most recent Caddy config reload. FAILED means the hub is still running the previous config — investigate via Caddy logs.

panels.title: Time since last reload
panels.description: Worst-case time since the last successful Caddy config reload across selected instances. A stale value here means at least one instance hasn't observed a reload — even if newer instances have.

panels.title: Subscribers connected (per instance)
panels.description: Subscriber count over time, broken out per hub instance. After an applied Caddy config reload the gauge excludes subscribers held over from the previous config until they disconnect.

panels.title: Connect / publish rate
panels.description: Subscriber accept rate vs update publish rate. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Disconnects by reason (rate/sec)
panels.description: Stacked rate of subscriber disconnects, labeled by reason. client_closed and write_timeout are the healthy steady-state reasons. write_timeout is the periodic recycle: each connection closes one dispatch_timeout before a deadline randomised to 80-100% of write_timeout (about 475-595 s with the defaults), or of the time left to the token's exp when that comes first. Sustained write_failed, transport_error or unknown rates indicate trouble; transport_error is recorded only when the subscribe loop exits without a classified reason (in practice a panic). transport_ended here means the subscriber could not keep up with its buffer. hub_shutdown, transport_ended caused by a reload or stop, and the write_timeout disconnects of a drain never appear in this panel: they are counted in the previous config's registry (reload) or after the :9091 listener closes (stop). Read them from the "Subscriber disconnected" log lines (reason attribute). Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Disconnect reasons (range share)
panels.description: Share of disconnects by reason over the selected range. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Disconnects by reason (range total)
panels.description: Disconnect counts per reason within the selected time range. Range-scoped, not since-process-start, so multi-instance restarts don't reset it. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Publish failures by reason (rate/sec)
panels.description: Stacked rate of publishes that failed, labeled by reason. validation = the update's content was rejected before dispatch (missing, too many or invalid topics, invalid retry, an update that fails validation, or an update too large for the transport to store, which answers 413); a client error, nothing stored. transport = any other dispatch failure (backend unreachable, write or codec error, transport closed during shutdown, or a deadline not caused by publish_timeout). timeout = dispatch aborted by publish_timeout (the 504 path). Pair with the publish-success rate in "Connect / publish rate". Auth rejections and unreadable or oversized request bodies are not counted here. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Claim-header rejections by reason (rate/sec)
panels.description: Rate of requests rejected by a require_claim_header binding. header_absent answers 400 for a missing bound header. malformed answers 400 for an empty or repeated bound header, or 401 for a bound claim of unusable type or shape. claim_absent (missing, null or empty claim) and mismatch answer 403. The malformed reason combines header and claim faults, so its count alone cannot distinguish 400 from 401. The binding label is the configured claim:Canonical-Header pair. Claim-value binding rejections are counted separately in the panel to the right. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Claim-value rejections by reason (rate/sec)
panels.description: Stacked rate of requests rejected by a require_claim_value binding, labeled by reason, with the HTTP status each answers: claim_absent (the claim was missing, null or empty; 403), mismatch (the claim holds none of the configured values; 403), or malformed (the claim has an unusable type or shape; 401). A value binding reads no header, so header_absent never occurs. These rejections are counted separately from the require_claim_header rejections in the panel to the left; split by the claim label to localize the binding. Counters restart at 0 on each applied Caddy config reload (every reload swaps in a fresh metrics registry); increments since the last scrape before the reload are lost.

panels.title: Subscribers by binding value
panels.description: The 10 largest binding values by connected subscriber count across selected instances. The binding is the claim:Canonical-Header pair of the require_claim_header binding with count_subscribers enabled, and the value is the header value it matched. Anonymous subscribers and bindings skipped by on_missing allow are not counted. There are no series until a subscriber is counted; a series is removed after its last subscriber disconnects. Hubs sharing a registry share these counts. topk is evaluated at each step, so more than 10 values can appear over a time range. After an applied Caddy config reload the gauge excludes subscribers held over from the previous config until they disconnect.

panels.title: SSE write+flush latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Write+flush latency of each SSE write to a subscriber (an update or a heartbeat comment): set deadline → Write → Flush → reset deadline. Filtered to outcome=ok so failed-write outliers (broken pipe in 200µs, deadline exceeded after dispatch_timeout) don't smear the percentile. Healthy steady state is sub-millisecond on a local network. Tail spikes here pair with the `Disconnects by reason (rate/sec)` panel (write_failed) and the `Write+flush rate by outcome` panel to localize hub-side stalls. Compare against mercure_redis_xreadgroup_latency_seconds on the transport dashboard to distinguish hub-side write back-pressure from transport-side poll latency.

panels.title: Write+flush rate by outcome
panels.description: Per-second rate of SSE write+flush observations (updates and heartbeat comments) split by outcome. A failed write ends its connection with a write_failed disconnect, so outcome=failed tracks the write_failed reason in the `Disconnects by reason (rate/sec)` panel one to one; a sustained rate means subscribers are dropping mid-stream (broken pipes, or writes stalled past dispatch_timeout). Pair with the `SSE write+flush latency (p50 / p95 / p99)` panel for the healthy-write tail.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Number of Go goroutines. SSE hubs grow ~1-2 goroutines per subscriber. Steady growth without subscriber growth indicates a leak.

panels.title: OS threads
panels.description: OS threads created by the Go runtime (go_threads) vs the GOMAXPROCS scheduler ceiling. go_threads can exceed GOMAXPROCS when goroutines block on syscalls; unbounded growth points at a syscall-blocking issue.

panels.title: Allocation rate
panels.description: Bytes allocated per second on the heap. Leading indicator of GC pressure — sustained high rate forces more GCs and longer pauses.

panels.title: Heap memory
panels.description: Live (heap_inuse) vs allocated (heap_alloc) heap, with GOMEMLIMIT overlay (only shown if set) and heap_released_bytes (returned to OS by the scavenger). heap_inuse - heap_released above 100 MiB after subscribers drain, with GOMEMLIMIT set, indicates real retention.

panels.title: Heap objects
panels.description: Number of allocated objects on the heap. Differentiates many small leaks from few large allocations — combine with Heap memory to triage leak shape.

panels.title: GC pause
panels.description: Garbage-collection pause distribution from Go's summary metric. Available quantiles are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 — max (1.0) is what blows SSE write deadlines under slow consumers.

panels.title: CPU rate
panels.description: Process CPU seconds per second. 1.0 (rendered as 100%) means one full core; values >100% indicate multi-core utilization.

panels.title: Resident memory (RSS)
panels.description: Process resident memory.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Open FDs vs the process's RLIMIT_NOFILE ceiling. Each SSE subscriber holds an FD — running near the ceiling will refuse new connects with EMFILE.

panels.title: FD utilization
panels.description: Worst-case fraction of the OS file-descriptor ceiling consumed (open / max). Each SSE subscriber holds an FD — sustained > 80% means new connects will start failing with EMFILE.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Process network bytes/sec — receive + transmit. SSE hubs are TX-heavy. process_network_* is exported on Linux only, so this panel is empty when the hub runs natively on macOS.

panels.title: Caddy admin requests
panels.description: Caddy admin API request rate by HTTP code (config reloads, health probes).

panels.title: Reverse-proxy upstreams healthy
panels.description: Count of healthy upstream backends served via Caddy reverse_proxy. Drops below configured replicas indicate one or more backends are failing health checks.

panels.title: GC pause vs write-failure disconnects
panels.description: Max GC pause overlaid with the rate of write_failed disconnects. A correlated spike points at GC pauses cascading through Caddy's write deadline machinery (a long pause stalls a write, the per-write deadline (dispatch_timeout) fires, the SSE handler reports write_failed). write_timeout is the routine periodic recycle, not a failure, so it is not plotted.

list.name: datasource
list.description: Prometheus datasource (matches the uid provisioned by `grafana/datasources.yml`). Required so the dashboard imports cleanly into Grafana instances whose Prometheus datasource has a different uid.
list.label: Data source

list.name: job
list.description: Prometheus scrape job for Mercure hub instances, sourced from `mercure_subscribers_connected` (always present, no startup-bind window). If empty, the hub is not being scraped — check Prometheus targets, not this dashboard.
list.label: Job

list.name: instance
list.description: Hub pod/replica identifier (Prometheus `instance` label). Use to scope panels to a single replica during incident triage; leave on `All` for fleet-wide views. Sourced from `mercure_subscribers_connected` (always present, no startup-bind window).
list.label: Instance
